A row's ValuePrefix is printed in front of its value, with a space, whenever there is a value to print. It is how the Rev cell reads 'Revision A' rather than a lone letter - Adam, 21-Sep-2026: 'it looks a bit silly with just a letter in'. It is PRINTED, never stored: the sheet still holds 'A', so the Drawing Register's column, the Sheet panel's box and the PDF file name's {revision} token (RevA) are all unchanged. A value that already starts with the prefix or a word it begins with ('Rev B', 'Revision B') keeps only the letter, so it can never print 'Revision Rev B'. An empty value prints nothing, prefix included. A prefix never costs another cell its text: on a strip too narrow for every value whole (A4 portrait) the builder solves it again with the bare values, and the cell prints 'A'.

Every row EXCEPT the Flex ones (the Drawing Title) is this much wider on the paper named - Adam, 21-Sep-2026: on A2 and A1 give the site address and each box on the right '20% more space', the drawing title excepted. Paper sizes not listed use the rows as they are. THE FIFTH IS ON WHAT THE CELL PRINTS AT, not on its WidthMm: RB05's address, 'West Beacon Farm, Deans Lane, Woodhouse Eaves, Leicestershire, LE12 8TE', had already grown its 70 mm cell to 84 to fit, and a fifth on the 70 would have been 84 again - no air at all for the one cell Adam pointed at; it is 100.8 now. THE EXTRA IS PAID ONLY OUT OF THE DRAWING TITLE'S SPARE ROOM, never out of its text: the cells take their fifth only while the strip still has room once every cell - the title included - has the wider of its WidthMm and its text; where it cannot afford all of it (A2 portrait, whose strip is A3 landscape's) every cell gets the same smaller share, down to none. On A2 landscape the fields are left 488 mm between the logo and the QR cell: 272 mm of fixed rows become 326.4, and the title keeps 161.6 of its 216. The logo cell and the QR cell are not rows and do not grow - the QR cell's width is measured to set its note in two even lines. The arithmetic is Na__LeTitleCells__Widen.

Listed in the order a job moves through them, which is the order both boxes offer. column3: THE RIGHT-HAND END OF THE STRIP IS THE PROJECT'S QR CODE AND A NOTE SAYING WHAT SCANNING IT DOES, so anybody holding a drawing can point a phone at it and be standing in the 3D model. It mirrors the logo cell at the left: an absolute width in paper millimetres off the end of the strip, the same on every paper, with the Rows solved across what is left between the two - so Status is the last FIELD and this cell stands beyond it, in the sheet's bottom right corner. It is modelled on Lantern Designer's terms cell, and at this strip height it is that cell's size: an 8.79 mm code with 0.61 mm round it. These keys say WHERE the code goes and how its note is set. WHAT it says - the address, the words, the symbol's colours, quiet zone and smallest readable module - belongs to the Project QR Code system: 02__Src__AppModules/53__Feature__ProjectQrCode/Na__ProjectQr__Config__.json. The code needs no size here: it is the strip's HeightMm less the quiet zone it is owed, so it follows the strip. With no project on the address bar, or with that system switched off, there is no cell and the fields keep the whole strip.
true

The whole cell: the note's column, then the code with its clear margin either side. The code and its margins take 10 mm of this, PaddingHMm and TextGapMm another 2.4, which leaves the note a column of 43.6 mm. MEASURED, NOT GUESSED: every width from 42 to 58 was wrapped against the shipped words in Open Sans at three body sizes, and this column is the one that sets the body at 1.5 mm in TWO LINES OF ALMOST EXACTLY EQUAL LENGTH - '...and view the building' over 'in full 3D, and to freely navigate and take a tour.' - flush without any letter spacing to speak of (0.004 mm). A millimetre either side wraps the same words into one long line and one short, or three with a widow, so re-measure if the words or BodyFontMm change. Lantern Designer's terms cell is 57. Never drawn narrower than the code and its margins, and never wider than a third of the strip, which is the logo cell's own cap.
The note stops this far short of the code's quiet zone. The zone alone is 0.61 mm, and a line of type ending that close to the symbol reads as touching it.

ON NARROW PAPER THE NOTE GOES BEFORE ANY FIELD IS CUT. If the whole cell would leave the fields less strip than this, the cell is drawn COMPACT instead: the code at its full size with Note CompactText turned up its left side, 12.4 mm wide in place of 56. Measured in Open Sans on 19-Sep-2026, a sheet's fields need from 193 mm at their text (PS01 with a short title) to 299 mm (a long client, three scales and an 84 character title). So 250 keeps the note on A3 landscape and everything larger - the fields are left 314 mm, which holds the worst of those whole - and drops it on A4 landscape and A3 portrait, where the whole cell would leave 191 mm and the compact one leaves 235; and on A4 portrait. The test is the paper's width and nothing on the sheet, on purpose: every sheet of one size in a pack is then drawn the same way, whatever its title runs to. 0 never goes compact.

The compact caption is bold, takes the labels' uppercasing and tracking, and reads upward, its baseline on the edge of the code's quiet zone and its capitals standing clear of it to the left. CompactPaddingMm is the clear paper between those capitals and the cell's rule. It has only the code's own 8.79 mm to run along: a caption that will not fit at CompactFontMm is set smaller rather than cut, because half an instruction is no instruction, and one that would have to go under CompactMinFontMm is left out altogether with the band it would have stood in - a code with no caption is still a code, and print too small to read is not a caption. The shipped '3D MODEL' fits at the full 1.6.

PaddingHMm is the fields' own FieldPaddingHMm, so the note starts where a field's label would. PaddingVMm is Lantern Designer's: the most the note's block may fill of the strip's height before it loses a line.

Lantern Designer's heading size, bold, with the labels' uppercasing and tracking, so the cell reads as part of the title block rather than as a sticker on it. The body is regular and muted, and 1.5 where Lantern's is 1.3: it is a lowercase sentence that a client has to be able to read, and two lines of it leave the strip room to spare. It inverts the caption-over-value rhythm of the field cells on purpose - those caption a value the reader is looking for, this one tells them to do something, so the instruction leads.

The most body lines ever set; fewer when the strip is too low for them (at 10 mm, three fit under the heading). Copy that will not fit ends in an ellipsis rather than overflowing the strip, which on a title block would read as a printing fault. The heading and body are centred in the strip's height as one block, measured from the top of the heading's capitals to the last baseline, so it sits level with the code beside it.
true

Every body line but the last is stretched to the column by letter spacing, so the note reads as a block with a flush right edge beside a square code (Lantern Designer's terms cell does the same). ALL OF THEM OR NONE: if any line would need more than JustifyMaxTrackingMm after every character, the whole block is left at its natural spacing - one flush line over one ragged one reads as a fault, where a wholly ragged block reads as a choice.

Locked scales for 2D viewports (D27). A viewport quotes one of these; the Viewport Settings panel shows one toggle button per scale, finest first (1:20, 1:50, 1:100, 1:200 - the last added 21-Sep-2026, for a whole building or a street on one sheet). The fallback list in Na__LayoutEditor__ConfigState__SheetSetup__.js mirrors this one: a saved scale that is on neither list is coerced to DefaultScaleDenominator on load, so the two must agree. A site plan viewport quotes one of SitePlanScaleDenominators instead. THE SITE PLAN LIST IS THE ONLY ONE THAT COUNTS: SitePlanExportConfig.SupportedScaleDenominators in the Tags SSOT is documentation and is read by nothing. A denominator of 500 or finer is a BLOCK PLAN, which draws the full fill / pattern / linework composite; coarser than 500 is a LOCATION PLAN, which draws only the proposed fills, no hatch patterns, and greyscales every line that is not a boundary or a proposal. THE SCALE ONLY DECIDES A VIEWPORT THAT HAS NOT BEEN TOLD: Viewport__SitePlan.SitePlan__PlanType overrules it, so a large site CAN be drawn as a block plan at 1:1250 and keep its patterns. The rule itself lives in Na__LayoutEditor__SitePlanComposites__Config__.json, which is what the app reads; the sentence here is the note beside the scales it applies to.

ROTATION (Viewport__RotationDeg, degrees clockwise). A selected viewport shows a round grip on a short stem off the middle of its top edge; drag it to turn the whole viewport - frame, drawing or picture, frame line and caption - about the middle of its frame, or type an angle in the Viewport panel's Rotation box. Shift holds a drag to RotateStepDeg steps counted from level (90: a quarter turn); without Shift a drag settles on a right angle once within RotateDetentDeg of one. RotateGripOffsetPx is how far off the top edge the grip stands on screen, at any zoom. Right-click a viewport for Rotate 90 degrees either way and Reset rotation. Nothing is rendered again for a turn - the picture and the linework are laid out in the frame's own axes and the frame is turned on the paper, and the PDF prints it turned. The key is written only while the viewport is turned, so a level viewport saves exactly as before.

Sheet dimensions (D32) drawn in paper millimetres. A dimension placed over a 2D viewport reports paper length times the viewport's scale denominator, so it measures the model. MEASURE AT SCALE (DefaultAtScale, the first control of the Dimensions panel, on by default): off every viewport a dimension reports the paper length times the sheet's scale - the scale its 2D viewports share, the biggest drawing's when they differ, the Scales default when it has none - so vectors drawn at scale measure true; switched off, a dimension reports paper millimetres wherever it is. Lengths typed into the Measurements box while one is placed are real sizes at the scale it will read. The record keeps the switch as Dimension__AtScale (true or false); a record from before it has no key and reports what it always did: the model on a viewport, the paper elsewhere. Precision is decimal places; the units suffix follows the figure. ORTHO: hold Shift while the line is being placed (after the second click) and the dimension runs horizontal or vertical whatever its two points are - drag the line above or below them for the x distance between them, beside them for the y. Release Shift and it is aligned again. The record keeps this as Dimension__Orientation ('aligned', 'horizontal' or 'vertical'; a record from before it is aligned). The offset is measured from the start point, and an ortho line stays where it was put while a grip re-picks either point. SIZE MM (TickLengthMm, MinTickLengthMm, MaxTickLengthMm): how large the ticks, arrows or dots at each end are, in paper millimetres. The Dimensions panel's Size mm row, under Ends, sets it per dimension; the record keeps it as Dimension__TickLengthMm. A record from before it has no key and draws at TickLengthMm. TEXT LEADER: click and drag the value off the line and a circular arc runs from the edge of the text back to the centre of the dimension line, tangent to the line there. Dimension__TextDXMm and Dimension__TextDYMm store the paper offset from where the value would have sat; dragging it back within TextLeaderMinMm snaps it home and both keys go. TextLeaderGapMm is the clear paper between the text box and the start of the arc. A record from before it has no keys and the value sits on the line as it always did.

DefaultExtensionMm is how far a new dimension's extension lines run back from the dimension line towards the points it measures, in paper millimetres; null draws the full lines. The Dimensions panel's Ext. lines row sets a start and an end length for each dimension, linked by the padlock between them, and the eyedropper copies them. The points themselves never move: a dimension still measures from them and they are still snap points.

ROUND UP (the Dimensions panel's Round up to 5 mm, under Units; OFF by default - DefaultRoundUp). On, a dimension's figure is raised to the next multiple of RoundUpStepMm at or above it - 6,413 reads 6,415, 6,416 reads 6,420 - and RoundUpMarker is printed straight after the figure (6,415* or 8,325* mm), so a rounded size is always marked. It rounds the figure the dimension would print at its own Decimals, so a size that reads exactly 2,810 stays 2,810 and carries no marker: only a figure the rounding actually raised is marked. An override is printed as typed, never rounded. The panel's Measures line keeps showing the exact figure. The record keeps the switch as Dimension__RoundUp, written only while it is on; a record from before it has no key and prints exactly as it did. RoundUpStepMm 0 rounds nothing.

AccordionSections are the sections that behave as one group. FocusSectionOnSelect: selecting something on the sheet, or picking a style with the eyedropper, opens that kind's section and folds the rest of the group, so what is on show is always what is being edited - a room opens Floor Areas, a site plan viewport opens Patterns, and any other viewport folds the whole group, its own section not being in it. Nothing selected leaves the folds as they are. Several can still be opened by hand to compare them; the next selection tidies them away again. CollapseOthersOnOpen goes further and folds the others the moment one is opened by hand.

HOW CLOSE, AND FOR WHOM - Adam, 21-Sep-2026: 'I can't get close enough into things... make an exception for the local host version'. The viewers do not need to zoom that far, and the live web should not have to keep drawing huge zooms. ZoomMax is a reader's ceiling: the web document viewer's, and any session's that may not author. AuthoringZoomMax is the ceiling wherever authoring is on - localhost, or a device unlocked with ?authoring=on - and is never taken below ZoomMax. Zoom 1 puts ScreenPixelsPerMm (3.2) screen pixels on a paper millimetre, so 8 is 25.6 px to the millimetre and 64 is 205: a 20 mm frame member drawn at 1:100 is 5 px across at 8 and 41 px at 64. Lines keep their printed weight as the sheet grows, as they do in LayOut; Draft mode (K) draws them one pixel wide at any zoom.

ZOOM NOW, REDRAW WHEN IT RESTS - Adam, 21-Sep-2026: 'there should be a debounce, so it waits a little bit after you stop zooming before it tries to redraw'. A wheel or pinch zoom only changes the paper's scale while it is under way; ZoomSettleMs after the last step the zoom 'settles' once, and everything that follows the zoom happens then, together: the selection handles and grips are counter-scaled again, the notes margin grip, group boxes, eyedropper boxes and the Measurements box are placed, Draft mode's hairlines are re-solved - and the sheet is drawn again, crisp, at its new zoom. Wheel steps are also gathered into one per animation frame. A single zoom (Fit, 100%, a resize) settles at once. 100 to 3000; LayOut's own Pan and Zoom Redraw Delay defaults to 300.

While a zoom gesture is under way the paper is held as one composited layer (will-change: transform), so each step scales the picture already drawn instead of rasterising every line, fill, hatch and picture on the sheet again; it is drawn crisp once, when the zoom settles. Measured on RB05's ground floor plan in headless Chrome: 76-110 ms a zoom step without it, 17-20 ms (50-60 frames a second) with it, zooming in and out alike. The sheet is soft while the wheel turns and sharp a moment after. False rasterises every step, as before.

The read-only document viewer the live web build shows in place of the editor. Where authoring is off - anywhere but localhost or an explicitly unlocked device - the drawing tabs, panel columns, toolbar and measurements box are never built, and the drawings and the project specification are shown as one cycled list of documents with a bar at the top and a dock at the bottom. Enabled false hands the web build back the read-only editor it had before this existed. ShowSpecification false leaves the specification out of the list entirely. column3: Object snaps for placing and dragging dimensions and vectors. Two sources: the projected linework inside 2D viewports, and - with SheetObjects on - the sheet's own vectors and dimensions, so a new line can start on the corner of the last one and a polygon can close exactly on its first point. A dragged vector snaps too: the grab point and every vertex are offered, and the nearest snap moves the whole shape. RadiusPx is the pick radius on screen at any zoom. Endpoints and midpoints are candidates; an endpoint wins a near tie, and the sheet's own markup wins a tie with the linework because it sits on top. The item being dragged never offers its own moving point. HiddenLines adds the hidden class as a source. The toggle (toolbar button or the Snap__Toggle key binding) is remembered per browser. MARKER COLOURS say which tool is snapping: blue for vertices (the Draw and Rectangle tools, vertex grips, and a vector being moved), orange for dimensions (the Dimension tool, its grips and its line inference), purple for viewports (carrying one by a point - the ring, the tracking crosses and the frame outline go purple too). The sheet's own paper as snap points (Adam, 21-Sep-2026: 'make points on the title block inferencible and snappable', to start construction lines from): the border's four corners and the middle of each side, the title block strip's corners, every cell divider's two ends and middle, and the notes margin's divider where it meets the border and the title block. A line drawn from the corner of the title block starts exactly there. Endpoints and Midpoints above still decide which kinds are offered; the classic scanned title block has no lines to offer.

Viewports move by a point, the way a block moves in CAD. With the Select tool, hover a 2D viewport's linework: the snap marker shows the point a press would carry it by. Drag, and that point snaps to every OTHER viewport's endpoints and midpoints (and the sheet's own vectors and dimension points). Rest the cursor on another drawing's point for AcquireDwellMs - before the drag or during it - and it is acquired as a tracking point (a small cross): the move then locks level with it or plumb below it, with a dashed guide, which is how two elevations line up side by side without being laid over each other. AcquireMax is how many are held at once, oldest dropped first; they are used up by the move they were acquired for, and Escape clears them. Shift holds the move to the nearer axis. ViewportCarry off makes every press move a viewport the plain way; ViewportTracking off keeps the point snap and drops the tracking. Needs Projected Linework on for the viewport being carried, since the points come from it. The snapping toggle switches all of it off.

{"LayoutEditor__ModelSource__Description": "Which design phase a viewport draws - the Model Source row of the Viewport panel, and the Model items on a viewport's right-click menu. The choices are the project's modelGroups (the existing building, a scheme, the next scheme); a viewport that names none draws the Project Default, which is the phase the 3D view opens with: the newest group whose label does not say 'existing'. Everything else stays the viewport's own - scene, cut, window, scale, render composites, model layers, edge styles - so a copy of a viewport switched to another phase is the same view of that model: an existing and a proposed elevation that line up exactly. A phase the 3D view does not hold is loaded off-scene the first time a viewport asks for it (the frame says so while it loads), with the same loader and materials as the 3D view, and goes into the scene only for the length of that viewport's render; the 3D view and the Design Phase menu are never touched. With OpenOnPlans on, a plan draws every door OPEN - in its linework, its base image and the PDF - whatever the 3D view shows, and the model's doors are put straight back afterwards. Each door opens exactly as a click in the 3D view opens it (the ADR / MOD / ROT naming contract): hinged leaves swing, bifolds fold, sliders slide. DrawSwings adds the arc each open hinged leaf's far edge sweeps, at the leaf's floor level and in the Doors layer's line style, one segment per SwingStepDegrees of swing; bifolds and sliders have no arc. With ClickToToggle on, a click on a door in the SELECTED plan viewport closes it and another click opens it again; a press that moves still moves the viewport, and each click waits ClickDelayMs so the two clicks of a double click (entering the content) leave the door alone. The right-click menu offers Close door or Open door for the door under the click, and Open all doors, whatever ClickToToggle says. A lock holds a viewport's frame, not what it draws, so the doors of a locked plan still close and open. Each change is one undo step. The record key is Viewport__ClosedDoors: the door keys drawn shut - an ADR name, or ADR::MOD for one leaf of an exterior double door, whose leaves open one at a time. With ShutOnElevations on, an elevation or section draws every door SHUT - in its linework, its base image and the PDF - whatever the 3D view shows, and has no door to click; off, it draws the doors as the model holds them. 3D viewports always draw the doors as the model holds them.", "LayoutEditor__PlanDoors__OpenOnPlans": true, "LayoutEditor__PlanDoors__ShutOnElevations": true, "LayoutEditor__PlanDoors__DrawSwings": true, "LayoutEditor__PlanDoors__SwingStepDegrees": 5, "LayoutEditor__PlanDoors__ClickToToggle": true, "LayoutEditor__PlanDoors__ClickDelayMs": 300, "LayoutEditor__PlanDoors__HideSwingsNote": "Hide swings, beside Open all on the Viewport panel's Doors row, leaves every door swing off ONE plan viewport - the arcs traced from its open doors AND the SketchUp door swing linework named in SwingCategoryKeys - in its linework, its base image and the PDF. How a press finds things on the paper. HitToleranceMm is paper millimetres at 100 percent (it shrinks as you zoom in); a drag starts past DragThresholdMm; grips are drawn GripSizePx square on screen at any zoom, and a picked one GripSizePickedPx so the points the next drag will carry read at a glance. A drag that starts where there is nothing to move - bare paper, the grey stage, a locked viewport - draws a selection box once it has travelled BoxStartPx on screen: dragged to the right a window (blue, solid edge) that takes only what it wholly encloses, dragged to the left a crossing (green, dashed edge) that takes anything it touches as well. BoxBorderPx is the box's edge weight on screen. BoxPreview outlines what the box would take while it is dragged, BoxPreviewPadMm clear of each item. The colours are in Na__LayoutEditor__Styles__Main__.css and the modifiers in Na__Hotkeys__DrawingTabs__.json.

column3: A press that PICKS is a pick first. The press that selects something, and the second press of a double click (one landing within DoubleClickSlopPx on screen and DoubleClickMs of the last, on the same item), has to travel PickDragPx on screen before it moves anything - so a pick with a wobble in it never nudges a note, and a fast double click always steps inside rather than shifting what it landed on. It applies where a double click means something: a whole-object move, a viewport's frame or content, a leader, a dimension's value. A press on something already selected moves at the ordinary DragThresholdMm, and vertices, measured points, crop handles and the rotate grip always do. DoubleClickMs should not be shorter than the operating system's own double click time (500 ms on Windows). PickDragPx 0 turns the longer travel off.
Type another distance to slide it again.
Drag the line to one side, then press Enter.
Drag the line clear of the drawing, then type how far off it should sit and press Enter. Type another distance to slide it again.

Editing inside a container, the way SketchUp works. Double-click (or press Enter on) a group to step inside it, and a vector to step inside that: while a container is open, only what is inside it answers a press, everything else on the sheet fades to FadeOpacity, and a vector's points are shown and can be dragged, boxed and added to. Click anywhere outside to step back out one level; Escape closes every container, drops the selection and puts the tools down. MoveToolRequired is the other half of the same idea: with it on, a whole object is only moved by the Move tool (M), so a stray drag with Select cannot shift a viewport or a note - grips, crop handles and the points of an open vector are still dragged by Select, because they edit an object rather than relocate it. Turn it off to have Select drag things about as it did before. GrabRadiusPx is how near a point of the open container a press has to land to be taken as a grab at it rather than the start of a selection box - screen pixels, so it is exactly as forgiving as the grip looks at any zoom. GripToleranceFactor widens the reach of a grip inside its own container, where nothing else is competing for the press: missing a corner by a pixel and dragging the whole object instead is what made dimensions feel untouchable.

column3: AutoMoveOnSelect is what stops MoveToolRequired being a chore. Selecting a note, a vector, a leader's bubble or a group is nearly always the first half of moving it, so a Select press on one of the AutoMoveKinds picks the Move tool up by itself and the same press can carry on into the drag. Kinds: annotation (text), shape (vectors), leader (its bubble, note or curve - never its endpoint, which re-points it and stays a grip), group (ordinary and parametric alike), and - left out on purpose - dimension and viewport, which still wait for M so a drawing or a measurement is never shifted by a stray drag. A Move that came up by itself goes back to Select by itself: on a press on anything not listed, when the selection empties, and when a double click steps inside a group, a vector or a text. Press M, or the Move button, for a Move that stays. Several selected items pick Move up only when every one of them is a listed kind. Turn AutoMoveOnSelect off to go back to pressing M every time.

Draw at scale - the first control of the Vectors panel, on by default. On, the sizes typed into the Measurements box while the Draw or Rectangle tool is up are real sizes at the drawing's scale: the scale of the 2D viewport under the first point, or the sheet's scale off every viewport (the scale its 2D viewports share, the biggest drawing's when they differ, the Scales default when it has none). 2500 at 1:50 draws 50 mm of paper, and a dimension measuring it at the same scale reads 2500 back. Off, typed sizes are paper millimetres. A setting of the drawing tools, not of a shape: a shape is paper points either way.

With Select or Move up, resting the pointer on a specification bubble's circle for NoteTooltipMs names its note beside the pointer - the code in bold, then the note's title (EW01  Loggia Arcade) - so a code can be read zoomed in, with the notes margin off the screen. A bubble linked to a note, or unlinked but reading a note's code, names it; one on a locked layer too, one on a reference layer not. Moving straight on to the next bubble names that one at once. The eyedropper (hotkey B) matches properties from one object on the sheet onto another. Click the object that already looks right, then click each object that should match it. StayLoadedAfterApply keeps the picked style on the dropper so a run of items costs one click each; with it off the dropper empties after the first apply and must be re-picked. CopyDimensionOffset is off on purpose: a dimension's offset is where its line sits, so copying it would move the target rather than restyle it. Style travels, content and geometry do not, and the layer never travels in any kind. Unlocked viewports match each other (render composites, frame, caption and scale); a locked viewport is not picked up at all, so the dropper reaches markup and other unlocked viewports through the frame. Shift+B is the palette mode: click an object and its style becomes the setting new objects of that kind are created with - the same traits travel, turned into the panel settings. PaletteSwitchesTool then hands over to the drawing tool for that kind (Text, Dimension, or whichever of Draw and Rectangle drew last); FlashMs is how long the item the style came from pulses.

A locked viewport (its own lock or its layer) is not a source and not a target, and the eyedropper does not resolve it, so a locked drawing is not detected over the markup on it. The Project Specification tab: every drawing note of the project, in groups. A group has a prefix (GN, SN, EE) and a title; a note has a title and its specification text. A note's code is its group's prefix and its place in the group, zero-padded to NumberDigits - GN01, EE02 - so moving a note up or down, moving it to another group or changing its group's prefix renumbers it. Specification bubbles on the sheets link to a note by its id, not its code, so a renumber reaches every bubble on every sheet. The specification is a file of its own (FileName) beside TrueVision__ProjectData__.json, kept locally in the project folder so an agent can edit it on disk, and written to the same R2 key on Sync. LegacyFileName is the previous R2 name, read only when FileName is not there yet. The file is read when the drawing editor opens. Every edit is kept in this browser at once (DraftEnabled, written DraftDebounceMs after the typing pauses); Sync writes the whole file to R2 and to the local copy, and first asks whether to replace a cloud copy that changed since it was read (ConfirmCloudOverwrite). HistorySteps is the tab's own undo depth.

Keeps the specification in the app and its local file (FileName) in step, as the Statement Writer does with a statement's markdown. Agents and hand edits change the local file directly, so on localhost the app looks at it on load, every LockstepPollMs while the drawing editor is open, when the window gets the focus back, and immediately before every write - the autosave, Enter in the drawing's Specification tab, Save Sheets and Sync. If the file no longer holds what the app last read or wrote, nothing is written and the app asks which copy to keep - its own (kept in this browser as a JSON draft) or the file - showing when each last changed and which notes differ. The copy not chosen is kept in this browser (Na__LayoutEditor__SpecDiscarded__<code>). What is in the app is written to the file AutoSaveLocalMs after the editing pauses (0 turns that off), so an agent always starts from what is on screen; R2 is still written only by Save Sheets and Sync. Whether the copies agree is decided by their content, not by each note's stamp; the times only explain. Set LockstepEnabled false to go back to the last save winning (the autosave to the file stops with it).

The notes margin a sheet can carry down its right-hand side, from the top of the border to the title block. The Measurements box at the bottom right of the sheet (Na__LayoutEditor__Measurements__), SketchUp's VCB. While the Draw, Rectangle or Dimension tool is up it reads out what is being drawn as it is drawn - a line's length, a rectangle's width x height, a dimension's span and then its line's offset - and a value typed while drawing is used on Enter, with no click into the box first: Draw places the next point that far along the rubber band (its direction, so snaps, Shift and the arrow key axis lock aim it); Rectangle lands the opposite corner (3000 x 2000 or 3000,2000; one figure is a square; typed straight after a rectangle lands, it resizes that rectangle); Dimension picks the end that far along the band, then puts the line that far from what it measures. Dragging a vertex of a finished vector wakes the box the same way: the reading is the drag's length, and a typed value moves the vertex that far along the inferred direction (the original vertex toward where it is being dragged; a minus sign runs the other way) and finishes the drag so the pointer cannot pull it back. Dragging a viewport's frame (not a handle, not the drawing inside) wakes it too: a typed value moves the frame that far along the drag, at the viewport's scale (or the sheet's for a 3D viewport). Moving a vector, a note, a leader, a dimension or a selection whole with the Move tool wakes it the same way, reading how far the move has gone as it goes (along an arrow-key lock, Shift or Ortho too). THE LAST MOVE STAYS IN THE BOX, as in SketchUp: when the button comes up, or a typed value lands the move, the box goes on reading it, and a length typed then lands it again exactly that far along the same line, measured from where it started - 1000, then 1200, then 1150 - until something else is selected, moved or changed, the tool changes or Escape is pressed. A vertex, a dimension end and a dimension line let go by the mouse stay typeable the same way. A typed value is absolute: no snap, grid, Shift or Ortho moves it. A number with no unit is millimetres; add m, cm or mm for another (2.5m), commas may group thousands (2,500) and a minus sign draws the other way. The line above the box shows how a value is being read as it is typed. AT SCALE: with Draw at scale on (Shapes DefaultAtScale) lines, rectangles and a dragged vertex take and show real sizes at the drawing's scale - the 2D viewport under the first point (or the vertex), or the sheet's scale elsewhere - so 2500 at 1:50 is 50 mm of paper; off, they are paper millimetres. A dimension uses Measure at scale (Dimensions DefaultAtScale). The chip at the right of the box shows the scale in use. Precision is the decimal places a reading shows (trailing zeros dropped), UnitsSuffix follows it, PairSeparator joins a rectangle's two sizes, HintMs is how long a message above the box stays, and EdgeGapPx keeps the box clear of the stage's scrollbars. The keys it reads are in Na__Hotkeys__DrawingTabs__.json under MeasurementsBox.
